q: A can complete a work in 10 days. What fraction of the work does he complete in one day?
exp: If the whole work takes 10 days, one day's work is 1/10 of the total work.

q: A can do a piece of work in 12 days. How many days will he take to complete the same work at the same rate?
exp: The time remains 12 days when the rate is unchanged.

q: A can complete a work in 8 days and B can complete it in 16 days. How long will they take together?
exp: Their daily work is 1/8 + 1/16 = 3/16. Time = 16/3 days, not 4 days. Therefore none of the listed options is exact.

q: If a worker completes a job in 20 days, what part of the job is completed in 5 days?
exp: Work completed = 5/20 = 1/4 of the job.

q: A can do a work in 15 days and B can do it in 15 days. How many days will they take together?
exp: Together their daily work is 1/15 + 1/15 = 2/15. Time = 15/2 = 7.5 days.

q: A worker earns ₹600 for 6 days of work. What is his daily wage?
exp: Daily wage = 600/6 = ₹100.

q: A can complete a work in 20 days. How many days will he need to complete half of the work?
exp: Half the work requires half the time: 20/2 = 10 days.

q: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours. What fraction of the tank does it fill in one hour?
exp: One hour's work is 1/6 of the tank.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours. How long will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
exp: Half the tank requires half the time: 8/2 = 4 hours.

q: A can complete a work in 10 days and B can complete it in 20 days. How much work do they complete together in one day?
If 5 workers complete a job in 12 days, how many worker-days are required for the job?
exp: Worker-days = 5×12 = 60.

q: A can do a work in 6 days. B is twice as efficient as A. How many days will B take?
exp: Twice the efficiency means half the time. B takes 6/2 = 3 days.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and another pipe fills it in 10 hours. How long do they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/10 + 1/10 = 1/5, so time = 5 hours.

q: A worker completes 1/5 of a job in one day. How many days are needed for the whole job?
exp: If one day's work is 1/5, the whole work takes 5 days.

q: Three workers receive ₹900 equally for a day's work. What is each worker's share?
exp: ₹900 ÷ 3 = ₹300 per worker.

q: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. How many days will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

q: A can do a work in 15 days and B in 10 days. In how many days can they complete it together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6. Therefore time = 6 days.

q: A can finish a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. If they work together for 6 days, what fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12. In 6 days they complete 1/2, so 1/2 remains. The correct option is 3rd, not the first.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. A alone can complete it in 12 days. How many days will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24. Thus B takes 24 days.

q: A can complete a work in 24 days and B can complete it in 16 days. If both work for 4 days, what fraction of the work is completed?
exp: Combined rate = 1/24 + 1/16 = 5/48. In 4 days, work = 20/48 = 5/12.

q: A is 50% more efficient than B. If B takes 18 days to complete a work, how many days will A take?
exp: A's efficiency is 1.5 times B's, so A's time = 18/1.5 = 12 days.

q: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they complete a work in 12 days. How many days will A alone take?
exp: Let B's rate be x, A's rate 2x. Together 3x = 1/12, so A's rate = 1/18. A takes 18 days.

q: A and B can complete a work in 10 days, B and C in 12 days, and C and A in 15 days. How many days will all three take together?
exp: Adding the three pair rates gives 1/10+1/12+1/15 = 1/4. This equals twice the combined rate of A, B and C, so their rate is 1/8. They take 8 days.

q: A can complete a work in 10 days. B can complete it in 15 days. If A works alone for 4 days, what fraction of the work remains?
exp: A completes 4/10 = 2/5. Remaining = 3/5.

q: A can complete a work in 18 days. B can complete it in 9 days. If B works alone for 3 days, what fraction remains?
exp: B completes 3/9 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours and B fills it in 18 hours. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and a second pipe empties it in 15 hours. If both are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30. Therefore the tank fills in 30 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours and another empties it in 12 hours. How long will the tank take to fill if both are opened together?
exp: Net rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24. Time = 24 hours.

q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 and 20 minutes respectively. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60. Time = 60/7 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. Due to a leak, the tank takes 8 hours to fill. How long would the leak alone take to empty the full tank?
exp: Leak rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = 1/24. Thus the leak alone empties the tank in 24 hours.

q: A can do a work in 16 days and B in 24 days. If they work together for 4 days, what fraction of the work is left?
exp: Combined rate = 1/16 + 1/24 = 5/48. Four days' work = 5/12, leaving 7/12.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 6 days. A alone takes 10 days. How long will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/6 − 1/10 = 1/15. B takes 15 days.

q: A worker is paid ₹1,500 for 5 days. At the same daily rate, how much will he earn for 18 days?
exp: Daily wage = 1500/5 = ₹300. For 18 days, wage = ₹5,400.

q: A and B complete a work together and receive ₹4,800. A does 3/5 of the total work. What is A's share?
A, B and C work for 6, 8 and 12 days respectively at the same daily wage. If the total wage is ₹5,200, what is B's share?
exp: Wage is proportional to days. Total days = 26. B's share = 8/26×5200 = ₹1,600.

q: A can complete a work in 30 days. B is 20% more efficient than A. How many days will B take?
exp: B's efficiency = 1.2 times A. Time = 30/1.2 = 25 days.

q: A is 25% less efficient than B. If B takes 16 days, how many days will A take?
exp: A's efficiency is 75% of B's. A's time = 16/0.75 = 64/3 days, about 21.33 days. None of the options is exact.

q: Four workers can complete a job in 15 days. Assuming equal efficiency, how many days will 5 workers take?
exp: Total work = 4×15 = 60 worker-days. For 5 workers, time = 60/5 = 12 days.

q: Six workers can complete a work in 20 days. After 5 days, two workers leave. How many more days will the remaining workers need?
exp: Total work = 120 worker-days. Work done in 5 days = 30 worker-days. Remaining = 90. Four workers need 90/4 = 22.5 days.

q: Eight workers can complete a work in 15 days. After 5 days, four more workers join them. How many total days are required?
exp: Total work = 120 worker-days. First 5 days complete 40. Remaining 80 is completed by 12 workers in 80/12 = 6⅔ days. Total = 11⅔ days.

q: A can do a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 3 days, after which A leaves. How many more days will B need?
exp: Together they complete 3×5/36 = 5/12. Remaining = 7/12. B's rate is 1/18, so remaining time = 7/12×18 = 10.5 days.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 20 minutes and B fills it in 30 minutes. If both are opened for 6 minutes, what fraction of the tank is filled?
exp: Combined rate = 1/20+1/30 = 1/12. In 6 minutes, 6/12 = 1/2 is filled.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 9 hours, while another fills it in 18 hours. If both are opened together, how much of the tank is filled in 3 hours?
exp: Combined rate = 1/9+1/18 = 1/6. In 3 hours, 3/6 = 1/2, so the correct option is the second.

q: A worker completes 60% of a job in 12 days. At the same rate, how many days are required for the entire job?
exp: If 60% takes 12 days, 100% takes 12/0.6 = 20 days.

q: A and B together can do a work in 12 days. B alone can do it in 20 days. How long will A alone take?
exp: A's rate = 1/12 − 1/20 = 1/30. Therefore A takes 30 days.

q: A can complete a work in 40 days and B in 60 days. If they work together for 8 days, what fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/40+1/60 = 1/24. In 8 days they complete 1/3, leaving 2/3.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 10 days. A alone takes 15 days. If B works alone for 4 days, what fraction of the work does B complete?
exp: B's rate = 1/10−1/15 = 1/30. In 4 days B completes 4/30 = 2/15, so none of the listed options is correct.

q: A can complete a work in 12 days, B in 18 days and C in 36 days. They work together for 4 days, then C leaves. How many more days will A and B need?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12+1/18+1/36 = 1/6. Four days complete 2/3, leaving 1/3. A and B rate = 1/12+1/18 = 5/36. Time = (1/3)/(5/36) = 12/5 days, so none of the options is exact.

q: A and B together complete a work in 8 days. A is 60% more efficient than B. How many days will A alone take?
exp: Let B's rate be x; A's rate is 1.6x. Together 2.6x = 1/8, so A's rate = 1/(20.8). A takes 20.8 days, so none of the options is correct.

q: A can complete a work in 20 days, B in 30 days and C in 60 days. A and B work for 6 days, then C joins them. How many total days are needed?
exp: A+B rate = 1/20+1/30 = 1/12. In 6 days they complete 1/2. A+B+C rate = 1/10. Remaining half takes 5 days. Total = 11 days.

q: A can complete a work in 24 days. B is 50% more efficient than A and C is 20% less efficient than A. How many days will all three take together?
exp: Let A's rate be 1/24. B's rate = 1.5/24 and C's = 0.8/24. Total rate = 3.3/24 = 0.1375. Time = 24/3.3 ≈ 7.27 days, so none of the options is exact.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours, B in 15 hours, and a leak empties it in 20 hours. If all are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/12+1/15−1/20 = 1/10. Therefore the tank fills in 10 hours.

q: Two pipes fill a tank in 12 and 18 minutes respectively, while a waste pipe empties it in 36 minutes. How long will all three together take to fill the tank?
exp: Net rate = 1/12+1/18−1/36 = 1/9. Therefore the tank fills in 9 minutes.

q: A and B can complete a work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. How many days will A, B and C together take?
exp: Adding pair rates: 1/12+1/15+1/20 = 1/5. This is twice the combined rate, so combined rate = 1/10. They take 10 days.

q: A can complete a work in 18 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 6 days. A then leaves. How many more days will B need?
exp: Together rate = 1/18+1/24 = 7/72. Six days complete 7/12. Remaining = 5/12. B takes (5/12)×24 = 10 days.

q: Eight workers can complete a work in 18 days. After 6 days, three workers leave. How many more days will the remaining workers need?
exp: Total work = 8×18 = 144 worker-days. Work done in 6 days = 48. Remaining = 96. Five workers need 96/5 = 19.2 days, so none of the options is exact.

q: A worker is 25% more efficient than another worker. If together they complete a job in 16 days, how many days would the less efficient worker take alone?
exp: Let the less efficient worker's rate be x. The other rate is 1.25x. Together = 2.25x = 1/16, so x = 1/36. The less efficient worker takes 36 days.
